method: Each section read in full by a machine-assisted reviewer against the packs and the ground catalogue as of this date; not a legal review.

sections.bearsOn: Defines park, conservancy, recreation area, designated wildland area, park use and resource use permits, and natural resources (land, water and their vegetable components, flora included), which makes timber in a park a protected natural resource; the park screen cites "natural resources".

The Act is subject only to the ELUA, the Environmental Assessment Act, the Wildfire Act (except s. 18) and a few others; ministers must exercise other powers, the Forest Act's included, only in accordance with it; the Heritage Conservation and Wildlife Acts apply in parks.
The minister manages parks, conservancies and recreation areas, their natural resources and the conduct of people in them.
Appointment of directors, officers and park rangers, who enforce the Act and the Wildlife Act.
Collaborative management agreements with governments and others.
Agreements with first nations for aboriginal rights activities and access in parks.

Cabinet establishes Class A, B and C parks, conservancies and recreation areas and designated wildland areas; conservancies are set aside for biodiversity, first nations' cultural uses and recreation, with development only consistent with those purposes; Schedule C and D parks and Protected Areas Act conservancies change only by statute.
Cabinet may have the minister manage land under an ELUA order, greenbelt land, heritage sites, recreation agreements, public trails and ecological reserves.
Cabinet may revise park, conservancy and recreation area boundaries, except those continued by the Protected Areas Act.
Boundaries may be described by official plans, metes and bounds or lot descriptions; written descriptions prevail.
Orders establishing or modifying parks must be published in the Gazette.

An interest in land in a Class A, B or C park or a conservancy may be granted or made the subject of a licence only by park use permit, and recreation area land is reserved from Land Act disposal except as the minister approves; a cutting or road permit cannot carry an interest in park land without one.

A natural resource in a Class A, B or C park, a recreation area or a conservancy must not be removed, destroyed or disturbed except by park use permit or the minister's approval, and never in a designated wildland area; no park use permit may authorize commercial logging in a conservancy.
sections.gapNote: The parks layer includes conservancies but no instrument screens the CONSERVANCY designation, where s. 9(10)(a) bars commercial logging outright; the park screen covers parks and recreation areas only.

sections.bearsOn: Park use permits may be issued for resort and tourism development consistent with a park's recreational values.
Park use permits may be issued for film production.
A park use permit may be issued for research, including feasibility studies for a road, pipeline or transmission line through a park, if consistent with its purpose.
Class C parks are run by park boards.

The minister may acquire land and timber rights for parks and expropriate mineral claims and leases and road-permit or special use permit roads; Crown land taken into a park is deleted from the timber supply area or area-based licence, with forest tenure compensation under Forest Act Part 18.
The minister may assign a park to a category, which limits its development.
No structure, improvement or work may be built in a park, conservancy or recreation area except under a park use or resource use permit; culverts, bridges and road works are caught.
sections.gapNote: The park screen's roads cell cites ss. 8 and 9 only; s. 13's bar on works and structures, and s. 16's on roads and log storage, are not cited.

sections.bearsOn: No garbage or waste may be transported through or deposited in a park except by permit.
All timber cut on or removed from a park, conservancy or recreation area must be disposed of under the Forest Act.

Except by park use or resource use permit, no one may use park, conservancy or recreation area land for a log storage area, mill site, road or right of way, obtain a surface right there, or exercise mineral, coal or petroleum rights there.
sections.gapNote: The park screen's roads cell cites ss. 8 and 9 rather than s. 16(a), which names roads, rights of way and log storage areas; a road crossing a park is flagged but not by this provision.

sections.bearsOn: Directors and park officers may inspect and order works altered or removed and conduct stopped.
Unperformed orders may be carried out at the person's expense.
No rights are acquired in resources or works taken or built in contravention; they may be seized.
The minister issues park use and resource use permits on fees and terms, with or without competition or public comment.
A park use permit may authorize a road through a Schedule F conservancy to reach natural resources beyond it.
A permit to remove or disturb natural resources needs an application and an undertaking to pay survey, cruise and inspection costs and fees.
A restoration deposit may be required before a permit issues.
Permits are not transferable without approval.
Improvements in a park belong to the government unless a permit says otherwise.
No property right in a park except by permit.
Lawful occupiers of government improvements in parks are exempt from tax on them.
The minister may accept gifts for parks and protected areas.
Administrative penalties for contraventions and permit breaches.
Compliance agreements reducing administrative penalties.
Recovery of administrative penalties.
Appeals of administrative penalties to the Environmental Appeal Board.
Offences: up to $1 000 000 and a year's imprisonment for contravening the Act.
Regulation-making powers for parks, including protection of flora, soil and waters.
Regulations on administrative penalties.
Sale of maps, merchandise and advertising.
Fees and charges for park use and services.

In a Schedule D park, existing permits continue by park use permit except for commercial logging, mining or hydro development; a range tenure in effect at establishment continues under the Range Act and FRPA, capped at the animal unit months then authorized.
Validates park use permits issued before 13 July 1995.
Permits may continue prior authorizations in a conservancy, except commercial logging, mining and hydro.
Repealed; no operative text.
Subsurface petroleum and natural gas rights may be granted under parks without surface access.
Nature conservancy areas continue as designated wildland areas.
Schedules A to F (no text stored).
